builder_plan.scenario: A product assistant retrieves plausible documents but gives unsupported answers.
builder_plan.change: Change one retrieval or ranking step while keeping the document snapshot fixed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retrieval pipeline with identical questions and answer model.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Supported answers, retrieval misses, correct abstentions, index cost, and response latency.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: The Intrusion Pathway: How Non-Evidential Context Degrades Language Model Performance
summary: The method replaces the default full attention computation under noisy, non-evidential context with a mask-level knockout of a small set of identified intrusion heads. It requires identifying those heads per model via activation analysis, adding a preprocessing step, and the ablation carries a bounded but nonzero cost to performance on helpful context. It can fail because head identification is model-specific, the 57% recovery is partial, and effectiveness on distractor types or tasks beyond the four evaluated is not established.
rationale: The intervention is cheap to apply at inference and directly addresses a common RAG failure mode, but it requires per-model head localization work and recovers only part of the degradation, so it warrants a workload-specific pilot before production adoption.
technique: Intrusion head knockout for noise robustness

claims.statement: The method replaces the default full attention computation under noisy, non-evidential context with a mask-level knockout of a small set of identified intrusion heads. It requires identifying those heads per model via activation analysis, adding a preprocessing step, and the ablation carries a bounded but nonzero cost to performance on helpful context. It can fail because head identification is model-specific, the 57% recovery is partial, and effectiveness on distractor types or tasks beyond the four evaluated is not established.
Ablating ~10 intrusion heads (~1% of attention heads) recovers 57% of the distractor-induced accuracy drop; an oracle residual replacement recovers 97.6% on average across four tasks.
